Warning Capability Notes

Updated: 2026-09-21

← Back to documents

Outlines trigger basis, alert levels, and configurable options for shoal, obstruction, off-course, speed-limit, prohibited-area, and bridge-clearance warnings.

WarningNavigation safety

Warning capability moves risk assessment ahead of the decision point: when a vessel approaches a hazard or drifts from the planned route, the system presents a readable alert instead of waiting for the operator to notice it.

Warning types and trigger basis

Warning typeTrigger basisPresentation
Shoals and shallow waterComparison of chart depth features with vessel draftLayer highlight with depth values
ObstructionsPositions of wrecks, rocks, and other obstaclesLayer annotation with key notes
Off-courseLateral deviation between planned route and live positionDeviation note with track trace
Speed-limit and prohibited areasNavigation rule areas and temporary noticesArea shading with entry reminder
Bridge clearanceClearance height, water level, and vessel air draftGraded alerts before approach

Alert levels

  • Informational: annotation and logging only, without interrupting the current operation.
  • Caution: layer highlight with text description to draw attention.
  • Alarm: sound or prominent prompt requiring human acknowledgement to continue.

Configurable options

  • Warning switches: enable or disable specific warnings by vessel type and water area.
  • Trigger thresholds: values such as under-keel clearance, off-course distance, and approach distance.
  • Presentation: combinations of text, shading, sound, and acknowledgement method.
Warning information is a navigation aid only. It does not replace professional judgment or statutory navigation responsibilities.
